"I keep saying I'll save what's left at the end of the month," Rehana said at the bank counter. "There's never anything left."
"Then let's not leave it to the end," Vinita said. "On the day your salary arrives, the bank can shift a set sum into a different savings account by itself. You won't need to remember."
"How much do I set?"
"An amount that doesn't hurt. Five thousand?"
Rehana hesitated, then nodded. "And I can change it later?"
"Any time."
Rehana signed the form. Two months later she came back to the same counter.
"It moved on the first, both times," she said. "I didn't even feel it."
Vinita smiled. "That's the point."

qa.a: It moves a set sum into a different savings account.

qa.a: Rehana was hesitant but hopeful, shown by the pause, the question about changing it later and the nod.

qa.a: Vinita sees it as a simple tool that removes the need to remember, and smiles when Rehana says the transfer did not hurt.

For two years I told myself I'd save whatever was left. Every month, around the 25th, there was nothing left. Not because I was reckless; small things just fill any empty space.
Yusuf, my flatmate, had a different system. By the evening his salary came in, a fixed amount had already gone into savings at another bank. "I never see it," he said. "So I never miss it."
In July I finally did the same. Twenty minutes on the bank's website: a standing instruction for the 1st of every month, the day my salary lands, into a savings account I have no card for.
The first month I noticed it. By the third, I didn't. Last week I checked the other account. Six months of transfers, and I had never once had to decide to save.
— Gautam

qa.q: When does Gautam's standing instruction run?
qa.a: On the 1st of every month, the day the salary lands.

qa.q: How did Gautam feel about the transfers by the third month?
qa.a: By then Gautam hardly noticed them and felt at ease, saving without any struggle.

qa.q: Why does using a separate account with no card help?
qa.a: It makes the money harder to spend on impulse, so it stays saved.
Yusuf sees it as automatic: he never sees the money, so he never misses it.

grounding: It shows someone setting a standing instruction to move a fixed amount to separate savings on salary day, so saving no longer depends on monthly willpower.

passage:
Employee wellness coach's note, 5 August.
Yogesh, from the logistics team, came to the money-habits session and admitted he had tried to save by willpower three times this year. Each time, by the 20th, the money was gone.
Instead of a budget talk, we did one thing. He logged into his bank on his phone and, with me beside him, set a standing instruction: a fixed amount moves into a separate savings account on the 1st, the day his salary arrives. He chose an amount he said wouldn't hurt, and he chose not to link that account to his debit card.
He laughed. "That's it? Five minutes?" I suggested he check the balance once a month but leave it alone.
Follow-up, 5 November: three transfers done, none reversed. He said the best part was not having to fight himself every month.
— Sonali

qa.a: On the 1st, the day his salary arrives.

qa.q: How did Yogesh feel after setting it up?
qa.a: He was amused and surprised, laughing "That's it? Five minutes?", and later relieved not to fight himself every month.

qa.q: What small choice made the plan stronger?
qa.a: Not linking the savings account to his debit card, so the money is harder to spend.

qa.q: How does Sonali see the change by November?
qa.a: Sonali sees three transfers done and none reversed: a habit that works without willpower.

grounding: It shows a young man setting up a standing instruction that moves a fixed amount to separate savings on salary day, removing the monthly need for willpower.
